cases.expected: JsonSchema instance representing the parsed schema (non‑null, no exception)
cases.description: Load a valid JSON Schema from the classpath using a null configuration, expecting a successfully built JsonSchema object.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) with default validation settings
cases.description: Load a schema from a file system path with an explicitly created default configuration; the factory should return a valid JsonSchema.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) where all $ref references are resolved during preload
cases.description: Schema contains internal $ref references; after getSchema the preload step must resolve them, so the returned JsonSchema is ready for validation without further loading.
Both parameters are null – the factory should reject the call and throw an IllegalArgumentException.
A null config should be treated as the default configuration; the method must still return a valid JsonSchema.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or IOException) indicating that the schema resource cannot be found
cases.description: The supplied SchemaLocation points to a resource that does not exist; the factory should fail with a clear exception.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or IOException) caused by network/IO failure
cases.description: A remote URI that cannot be resolved should cause the factory to throw an exception rather than returning a null schema.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) with circular $ref resolved without stack overflow
cases.description: Two schemas reference each other (circular $ref). The preload step must detect and handle the cycle, returning a usable JsonSchema.

cases.expected: Two successive calls return the same JsonSchema instance (==)
cases.description: JsonSchemaFactory caches loaded schemas; calling getSchema twice with the same location and config should return the identical object.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) where type‑loose validation is enabled
cases.description: When the config enables typeLoose, the created JsonSchema must reflect this setting; subsequent validation would allow type coercion.

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance (non‑null) where type‑loose validation is disabled
cases.description: Same schema but with typeLoose disabled; the factory must honour the config and produce a schema that enforces strict typing.
The schemaUri argument is null while a non‑null configuration is supplied; the factory must reject the call and throw IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or JsonSchemaException) indicating unsupported URI scheme
cases.description: A SchemaLocation using an unsupported protocol (ftp) is provided; JsonSchemaFactory should fail early with an appropriate exception.
The URI string is syntactically malformed; the factory must detect the problem and throw IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or IOException) caused by parsing failure
cases.description: The resource exists but contains plain‑text (non‑JSON/YAML) data; reading it as a schema should raise a parsing‑related exception.
The file is valid JSON but does not conform to JSON‑Schema syntax (e.g., unknown keyword, wrong type); the factory must throw a JsonSchemaException during loading.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or IOException) caused by missing $ref target
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref that points to a non‑existent external schema; preload should detect the missing reference and raise an exception.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or JsonSchemaException) indicating unknown meta‑schema IRI
cases.description: The schema declares a $schema IRI that the factory does not recognise; loading must fail with an appropriate exception.
